candidate.title: SMORE-Seq
candidate.scope: The SMORE-Seq row of the assigned Illumina poster, from depicted capped mRNA through adapter-flanked cDNA, interpreted against the poly(A)+ yeast SMORE-seq implementation described by Park et al. (2014). The fragmented preparation is shown as several molecular classes within one route; its 5′-tagged class is retained at the final endpoint. The paper clarifies the contribution of pre-existing phosphorylated degradation products to PAS reads and the limitations of cap-based TSS selection. PEAT, TL-seq, partial TIF-Seq and the chemical legend are neighboring context, not target alternatives. The independently checked collection-page heading and schematic description identify the same target. Sequencing and the paper’s TAP− controls are readout context, outside the drawn operation graph.

states.label: Poly(A)+ RNA population, depicted as capped mRNA
features: The input cartoon is a purple RNA with a 5′ GPPP cap and a 3′ AA(A)n tail; the small RNA icon beside the method name is explanatory, not an additional input branch.
The inspected primary implementation uses poly(A)+ RNA from S. cerevisiae total RNA. Its isolation is preparation history, not an added operation in the assigned drawing.

Primary-source clarification: the population can also contain pre-existing uncapped 5′-phosphorylated degradation intermediates. The authors infer their contribution to PAS reads; the capped-only cartoon does not show them.
No phosphatase pretreatment is present in this scoped route, allowing pre-existing 5′ phosphates to remain ligatable.

states.label: Fragmented RNA population with distinct adapter histories
features: The broken RNA cartoon and next panel distinguish three representative classes in the same preparation: an original 5′ fragment carrying green adapter; a poly(A)-bearing 3′ fragment lacking green adapter; and an internal fragment lacking green adapter.
Fragmentation occurs after 5′ adapter ligation. Newly created fragment ends therefore do not acquire the green adapter in this operation.
The displayed fragment classes are constituents of a fragmented preparation, not separately prepared samples or a depicted pooling event.

The paper-supported PAS-bearing contribution must arise from an already 5′-tagged substrate that retains its poly(A) junction in a library fragment; the generic newly separated poly(A) fragment is not automatically adapter-complete.

states.label: Retained adapter-flanked cDNA library
features: The final cDNA icon is a blue duplex with green and orange terminal adapter sequences.
The sequenced material is RNA-derived DNA; biological targets are transcript 5′ boundaries and polyadenylation junctions.
In the primary interpretation, cap-derived read starts support TSS identification after accounting for background. Reads spanning an untemplated poly(A) junction support PAS identification.
TSS and PAS are identified separately from the same RNA population; this library does not provide a per-transcript pairing of its original 5′ and 3′ ends.

PAS-bearing degradation intermediates are the authors’ explanation for the 3′ signal, not proof that every retained molecule originated at a cap or that every poly(A)-bearing cleavage product is sequenced.

corrections.diagram_observation: The input is shown only as capped polyadenylated mRNA. The generic poly(A)-bearing 3′ fragment created after fragmentation lacks green 5′ adapter, while the final retained cDNA has green and orange ends. The drawing alone therefore does not explain the stated simultaneous mapping of both RNA ends.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper reports ligatable 5′-phosphorylated degradation products and explicitly links their recovery to omission of phosphatase pretreatment; it hypothesizes these products as the origin of PAS-bearing reads. The authored input-population state and downstream information effects include that primary-supported substrate class while preserving the drawn order. No new 5′ adapter ligation is assigned to generic post-fragmentation 3′ fragments, and no same-molecule TSS–PAS linkage is claimed.
